thread:
Mira (Design): Quick idea 1-line role summary under name + three priority permission chips, full matrix behind an expand. Mock: https://staging.redwood.design/snap-v4 :sparkles:
Eli (PM): Goal: reduce scanning time and surface default invite role in the invite modal. Avoid vague labels like 'Admin'. Use verbs.
Kao (Frontend): Agree. Technical notes: return "priority_permissions" from API to keep client cheap for large orgs. Chips should be buttons with aria-pressed.
June (Accessibility): Chips must not rely on color alone. Add icons + visible text and aria-describedby that reads the verb list. Ensure focus order: expand chevron next after role name.
Rory (Research): In quick tests users looked for verbs. Plan: run 6 admins + 3 screen reader users with tasks: find who can remove members, open permission history, invite with default role.
Mira (Design): Microcopy: "Key perms: Manage billing  Remove members  Manage apps". Invite modal header: "Default role for new invites: <Role>  change". SSO toggle label: "Require SSO for all sign-ins" with tooltip "Disables email/password sign-in when enabled."
Kao (Frontend): Audit deep-link pattern: /orgs/:orgId/audit?role=:roleId&event=permission_change. Keyboard shortcut idea: focus role -> press "." then "h" to open history. We'll list shortcut in help modal.
June (Accessibility): When history opens announce via aria-live: "Permission history opened for <Role>". Expansion should set aria-expanded and move focus to first permission.
Mira (Design): Action items:
- @Kao: add chip semantics + API flag (ETA Tue)
- @June: publish a11y checklist + aria copy (ETA Mon)
- @Rory: recruit participants + script (ETA Thu)
- @Eli: finalize invite + SSO microcopy (ETA Wed)
